preamble: Fortition of the lateral approximant [l] to the voiced alveolar lateral fricative [ɮ] adds turbulent airflow while keeping the lateral channel. Khalkha Mongolian has no lateral approximant: Proto-Mongolic *l is a fricative /ɮ/ (often devoiced to [ɬ]), while Chakhar keeps [l]. In Yami (Tao) of Orchid Island, /l/ is realized as [ɮ] before the high front vowel /i/, an allophone that younger, Mandarin-dominant speakers are replacing with [l].
sources: Svantesson, J.-O., Tsendina, A., Karlsson, A., & Franzén, V. (2005). The Phonology of Mongolian. Oxford University Press. https://global.oup.com/academic/product/the-phonology-of-mongolian-9780199260171
